facts.statement: The dinosaur Buitreraptor was first described in 2005, with Buitreraptor gonzalezorum as its type species.
facts.quote: Buitreraptor was described in 2005 and the type species is Buitreraptor gonzalezorum.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) in Argentina within the Candeleros Formation.
facts.quote: Buitreraptor (meaning "La Buitrera seizer") is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaurs that lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) of Argentina at the Candeleros Formation.

facts.statement: Four specimens of Buitreraptor were discovered in 2004 in Patagonia, Argentina, during an excavation led by Sebastián Apesteguia and Peter Makovicky.
facts.quote: Four specimens of Buitreraptor were found in 2004 in sandstone in Patagonia, Argentina during an excavation led by Sebastián Apesteguia, researcher of CONICET at the Fundacion Felix de Azara - Maimonides University, and Peter Makovicky, curator of dinosaurs at the Field Museum in Chicago.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor fossils were found at the La Buitrera site, which translates to "vulture roost".
facts.quote: It was uncovered in a famous fossil site named La Buitrera, the "vulture roost".

facts.statement: The genus name Buitreraptor means "vulture raider," combining the Spanish word for vulture and the Latin word for seizer.
facts.quote: The genus name means "vulture raider", from the Spanish word buitre meaning vulture, in reference to La Buitrera, and Latin raptor, "seizer".

facts.statement: The specific name gonzalezorum honors the González brothers, Fabian and Jorge, who performed much of the excavation and preparation work.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the González brothers, Fábian and Jorge, who realised much of the actual excavation and preparation of the fossils.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Buitreraptor measured 1.5 meters in length and weighed three kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 1.5 metres, the weight at three kilograms.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor had a slender, flat, extremely elongated snout with small, grooved, strongly recurved, and flattened teeth lacking meat-tearing serrations.
facts.quote: Buitreraptor has a slender, flat, extremely elongated snout with many small teeth that lack meat-tearing serrations or cutting edges and are grooved, strongly recurved and flattened.

facts.statement: Scientists concluded that Buitreraptor hunted small animals like lizards and mammals rather than large prey.
facts.quote: From this, the scientists who initially described it concluded that this dinosaur was not a hunter of relatively large animals like some other dromaeosaurs, but rather a hunter of small animals such as lizards and mammals.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor had long forelimbs ending in very long and thin three-fingered hands.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Buitreraptor were long and ended in very long and thin three-fingered hands.

facts.statement: Although no feathers have been found on Buitreraptor fossils, it is likely the dinosaur was feathered based on evidence from its close relatives.
facts.quote: No fossil discoveries have been made of any feathers of Buitreraptor. However, there are relatives like Microraptor and Sinornithosaurus, of which fossils with preserved feathers are known. Since its close relatives had feathers, it is likely that Buitreraptor also was feathered.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor was assigned to the family Dromaeosauridae and the subfamily Unenlagiinae in 2005.
facts.quote: It was in 2005 assigned to the Dromaeosauridae. A cladistic analysis by the describers showed it was part of the dromaeosaurid Unenlagiinae.

facts.statement: Unenlagiines, including Buitreraptor, were better adapted for running and pursuit predation than the stockier Laurasian dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Unenlagiines had better capacities for running and pursuit predation than other dromaeosaurids such as Laurasian dromaeosaurids (Eudromaeosauria), which were more stocky and had shorter legs and had an active predatory lifestyle.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor likely swallowed prey whole because its teeth lacked serrations and functioned only to hold food.
facts.quote: Buitreraptor probably swallowed its prey whole due to its lack of serrated teeth with flesh-tearing capabilities; the teeth functioned to simply hold prey.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 92 to 95 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 92 y 95 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense-Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor had an extremely elongated, flat snout that was 25% longer than its femur, containing narrow, grooved, strongly recurved, and flattened teeth without serrated edges.
facts.quote: Poseía un hocico esbelto, plano, extremadamente alargado, un 25 % más que el fémur y estrecho con los dientes que carecen el borde aserrado para rasgar carne y están ranurados, fuertemente recurvados y aplanados.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor had long forelimbs ending in hands with three fingers.
facts.quote: Los miembros anteriores eran largos y terminaban en manos con tres dedos.

facts.statement: Unlike most relatives where the second finger was significantly longer, Buitreraptor's three fingers were proportionally shorter and essentially equal in length.
facts.quote: Los dedos eran proporcionalmente más cortos que en otros dromeosáuridos, y esencialmente de la misma longitud, contrariamente a la mayoría de sus parientes, que tenían dedos de longitud diferente, con el segundo dedo siendo considerablemente más largo.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor had a very elongated body with a shallow chest and hind legs adapted for running that ended in a retractable claw.
facts.quote: El cuerpo como un todo también era muy alargado, con una caja torácica poco profunda y patas traseras aptas para la carrera que terminaban en una garra retráctil.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor is estimated to have reached a length of 1.20 meters, a height of 40 centimeters, and a weight of 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Se calcula que llegó a medir 1.20 metros de largo, 40 centímetros de alto y a pesar 5 kilogramos.

facts.statement: No fossil feathers have been discovered for Buitreraptor, though it likely possessed them based on its phylogenetic position.
facts.quote: No se han hecho descubrimientos fósiles de ninguna pluma de Buitreraptor.

facts.statement: Four Buitreraptor skeletons were found between 2001 and 2004 in the Candeleros Formation, dating to approximately 94 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Cuatro esqueletos de Buitreraptor fueron hallados a lo largo de varios años entre 2001 y 2004 en las areniscas eólicas de la formación Candeleros, que data entre el Cenomaniano y el Turoniano, hace aproximadamente 94 millones de años en el Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor was discovered during an excavation led by Sebastián Apesteguía and Peter Makovicky.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto durante una excavación dirigida por Sebastián Apesteguia, investigador del CONICET en la Fundación Félix de Azara, Universidad Maimonides sumándose al equipo Peter Makovicky, curador de dinosaurios del Museo Field de Historia Natural.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor fossils come from the La Buitrera site in Río Negro province, northern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos de Buitreraptor provienen del famoso sitio fósil llamado La Buitrera, el "refugio del buitre" en la provincia de Río Negro, en el norte de la Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor was first described and published in the journal Nature in 2005.
facts.quote: Su descripción se publicó en la revista Nature en 2005.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPCA 245 is a nearly complete articulated adult skeleton housed at the Museo Provincial Carlos Ameghino in Cipolletti, Argentina.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MPCA 245, se encuentra en el Museo Provincial Carlos Ameghino de la ciudad de Cipolletti, provincia del Río Negro, Argentina, consistiendo en un esqueleto casi completo, articulado de un adulto.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor gonzalezorum is the only known species within the genus Buitreraptor.
facts.quote: Buitreraptor gonzalezorum es la única especie conocida del género Buitreraptor.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor was assigned to the family Dromaeosauridae in 2005.
facts.quote: Fue en 2005 asignado a la familia Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis by its describers showed that Buitreraptor belongs to the subfamily Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico por los descriptores mostró que era parte de la subfamilia Unenlagiinae.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor exhibits a mosaic of traits found in dromaeosaurids, troodontids, and avialans.
facts.quote: Buitreraptor muestra un mosaico de rasgos de dromeosáurido, troodontido y avialano.

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether flight evolved independently in birds and dromaeosaurids or was derived from a common flying ancestor, a question raised by the discovery of Buitreraptor.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Buitreraptor también ha sido objeto de discusión entre los científicos en cuanto a la cuestión de si el vuelo podría haber evolucionado independientemente en aves y dromeosáuridos o fue derivado de algún ancestro común volador.

facts.statement: Buitreraptor lived approximately 94 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: hace aproximadamente 94 millones de años en el Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: Initial researchers concluded that Buitreraptor hunted small animals like lizards and mammals rather than large prey like some other dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Los científicos que lo describieron inicialmente concluyeron que este dinosaurio no era un cazador de animales relativamente grandes como lo eran algunos otros dromeosáuridos, siendo un cazador de pequeños animales como lagartos y mamíferos.

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis suggests dromaeosaurids originated in Laurasia and migrated to Gondwana during the Cretaceous, as southern species possess distinct traits not shared by northern relatives.
facts.quote: Los científicos lo ven como una posibilidad alternativa de que los dromeosáuridos se originaron en el antiguo continente Laurasia en el norte y durante el período cretácico emigraron al sur de Gondwana, ya que las especies conocidas del hemisferio sur tienen características distintivas no compartidas por sus familiares del norte.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range for Buitreraptor as the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)
